To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the nonlinearity, the number of terms and the restriction of a Boolean function to a coset are closely related to each other and (2) quadratic terms in the algebra normal form of a Boolean function play an important in the determination of the nonlinearity.

(1) nonlinearity of functions is related to the distribution of terms and cycles of odd length, (2) nonlinearity is related to the number of terms of the function, and (3) restrictions of a function have a significant impact on nonlinearity of that function.
the nonlinearity and the number of terms of a function, are closely related to the restriction of the function on cosets, and the distribution of the terms in its algebraic normal form.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the nonlinear characteristics of Boolean functions?
the nonlinear properties of (Boolean) ciphers and encryption algorithms.
the study of nonlinear properties of Boolean functions, in particular, nonlinearity and the number of terms of a function, as well as restrictions of a function to cosets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nonlinearity and the number of terms of a function are not necessarily related, and the nonlinearity can be increased by reducing the number of terms.
the nonlinearity, the number of terms and the restriction to cosets of a function are all closely related to the nonlinear characteristics of a function.
the nonlinearity, the number of terms as well as the distribution of terms of a function are closely interrelated and are of great importance in the design of ciphers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonlinear characteristics of a function can be studied from different perspectives and the results obtained in this work can be used in the design or cryptanalysis of ciphers.
we have provided a new and more systematic way to understand nonlinear properties of functions, and that our results are of practical importance in the design and security of ciphers.
the nonlinearity, terms, and restriction of Boolean functions are closely related to each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the nonlinearity and the number of terms of a Boolean function can be used as measures of security against some attacks, and the number of quadratic and odd-length cycles in the algebraic form of the function can be used for estimating nonlinearity.
the restriction of the function, and the distribution of the terms in the ANF, are important parameters that should be taken into account in the construction of ciphers and encryption algorithms.
a function should be designed to be resistant to attacks that exploit its nonlinear characteristics, which can be achieved by controlling its terms in the algebra normal form.
